title: Joining a monomorphism with a weakly contractible simplicial set is right anodyne
statement: Use simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. For simplicial sets $X,Y$ define their join by $(X\star Y)_n=X_n\amalg Y_n\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=n}X_a\times Y_b$, where $a,b\geq0$; simplicial operators restrict the initial block of $X$-vertices and final block of $Y$-vertices, with empty blocks giving the pure-factor summands. Let $u:A_0\hookrightarrow A$ be an inclusion of small simplicial sets and let $B$ be any small simplicial set such that $B\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Then $u\star\operatorname{id}_B:A_0\star B\hookrightarrow A\star B$ is right anodyne. No Kan or quasicategory hypothesis is imposed on $A_0,A,B$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.3.6, printed p. 251 (with Lemma 4.2.3.5 for its proof). No Stacks tag for this infinity-categorical anodyne lemma.

proof.text: By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], weak contractibility means that $|B|$ has one path component and its based homotopy groups are trivial. In particular $|B|$ is nonempty. Its realization quotient has a representative belonging to $B_n\times|\Delta^n|$ for some $n$, so restriction to a vertex of that simplex gives $b\in B_0$. The vertex map $\Delta^0\to B$ is degreewise injective, since its domain has one simplex in each degree. Its realization induces the bijection between the singleton sets of path components and, at its unique base point, isomorphisms between trivial homotopy groups in every positive degree. Thus $j:\{b\}\hookrightarrow B$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Here $\{b\}$ means the simplicial image of the vertex map, including all its degeneracies, and is isomorphic to $\Delta^0$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.6, printed p. 251: nonemptiness and the chosen vertex weak equivalence; expanded directly from the realization definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cone-mono-right-anodyne] to the degreewise injective $u:A_0\hookrightarrow A$. Let $e:\Delta^0\to\{b\}$ be the isomorphism sending the unique simplex in degree $n$ to the $n$-fold degeneracy of $b$. For $X=A_0,A$, define $\alpha_X:X\star\Delta^0\to X\star\{b\}$ by the identity on the pure $X$ summand, $e$ on the pure point summand, and $(x,t)\mapsto(x,e(t))$ on each mixed summand. These formulas commute with the block-restriction operators, and replacing $e$ by $e^{-1}$ gives their inverses. They give a commutative square from $u\star\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0}$ to $u\star\operatorname{id}_{\{b\}}$. This square is a pushout: for maps $s:A\star\Delta^0\to T$ and $t:A_0\star\{b\}\to T$ agreeing on $A_0\star\Delta^0$, its unique extension is $s\alpha_A^{-1}$, whose restriction is $t$ by commutativity and the agreement. Thus $A_0\star\{b\}\hookrightarrow A\star\{b\}$ is right anodyne by pushout closure in [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Put $P=(A_0\star B)\amalg_{A_0\star\{b\}}(A\star\{b\})$. Degreewise the two indicated subsets of $A\star B$ intersect in $A_0\star\{b\}$: the pure $A$ intersection is $(A_0)_n$, the pure $B$ intersection is $\{b\}_n$, and each mixed intersection is $(A_0)_a\times\{b\}_b$. Maps on their union are exactly maps on both subsets agreeing on this intersection, degree by degree and compatibly with operators. Hence this union is their simplicial pushout, and $A_0\star B\hookrightarrow P$ is right anodyne by a second use of the same pushout closure.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.6, printed p. 251: point-factor case and first pushout inclusion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-join-pushout-right-anodyne] with $i=u$ and $j:\{b\}\hookrightarrow B$ from Step 1. Both are inclusions of small simplicial sets, and Step 1 proved the required weak homotopy equivalence. Its displayed source is exactly $P$ of Step 2. Consequently $P\hookrightarrow A\star B$ is right anodyne.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.6, printed p. 251: apply Lemma 4.2.3.5 to the second inclusion.

proof.text: Put $Z_0=A_0\star B$, $Z_1=P$ and $Z_2=A\star B$, with the inclusions of Steps 2 and 3. The composite fixes the pure $B$ summand, acts by $u$ on the pure $A_0$ summand, and sends $(a,b)$ to $(u(a),b)$ on every mixed summand. It is therefore $u\star\operatorname{id}_B$. The ordinal chain $(Z_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq2}$ has two successor arrows and no nonzero limit stages. Thus the transfinite-composition closure of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne] makes its composite right anodyne.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.2.3.6, printed p. 251: composition of the two inclusions.
